skill.name: pydicom
skill.description: Guidance and helper scripts for reading, converting, anonymizing, and extracting metadata from DICOM medical imaging files with pydicom.
skill.summary: Work with DICOM medical imaging files using pydicom workflows and helper scripts.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, pydicom documentation URLs, and DICOM terminology. The real concern is patient privacy: the helper scripts can export PHI and the anonymizer is not a complete DICOM de-identification workflow. No prompt injection or covert network behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Implement a recognized DICOM de-identification profile, handle private tags, regenerate UIDs when appropriate, and add checks for burned-in identifiers.
Add a redact-by-default mode, provide an allowlist of safe fields, and warn users before writing patient metadata to files.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete DICOM De-identification Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The anonymization helper removes a fixed list of PHI tags but leaves UID regeneration commented out before saving the file. DICOM files can also contain private tags and burned-in identifiers that this workflow does not detect.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code shows a fixed PHI tag list and UID anonymization disabled in comments. This is a clear privacy gap for medical imaging data.

semantic_findings.title: Metadata Export Can Reveal Patient Data
semantic_findings.description: The metadata extractor prints patient fields and can export all non-sequence DICOM elements to a user-selected file. Those exports can contain PHI if users share them without redaction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly includes PatientName, PatientID, and related fields, then writes extracted metadata to disk when requested.

content.user_title: Process DICOM Medical Imaging with pydicom
content.value_statement: DICOM files contain complex imaging data and sensitive metadata that are hard to inspect safely. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pydicom workflows for reading, converting, anonymizing, and extracting metadata.
actual_capabilities: Read DICOM files and inspect standard dataset attributes.
Extract pixel arrays for CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, and related modalities.
Convert DICOM pixel data to PNG, JPEG, or TIFF with helper guidance.
Remove or replace common PHI tags with the anonymization helper script.
Extract selected or full DICOM metadata as text or JSON.
Explain transfer syntaxes, compression handlers, and decompression workflows.
limitations: Anonymization is not a certified de-identification process and must be verified before data sharing.
Pixel data can contain burned-in identifiers that metadata removal does not detect.
Compressed images may require optional libraries such as pylibjpeg or GDCM.
Clinical use requires expert validation and compliance review.

use_cases.title: Inspect Imaging Metadata
use_cases.description: Review modality, dimensions, study details, and transfer syntax before processing a DICOM dataset.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Copies
use_cases.description: Create working copies with common patient identifiers removed, then verify them before sharing.

use_cases.title: Build Image Pipelines
use_cases.description: Convert pixel data, handle compressed images, and preserve spatial metadata for downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a DICOM File
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect this DICOM file with pydicom. Summarize modality, image size, transfer syntax, and any patient identifiers I should protect.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Images for Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through converting a folder of DICOM images to PNG while applying appropriate windowing and preserving the original files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Research Copies
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me anonymize DICOM files for research. Identify PHI fields, UID handling needs, and verification steps before export.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch pydicom workflow that reads a study series, validates transfer syntaxes, extracts safe metadata, and records processing errors.

output_examples.input: A user asks to summarize one CT DICOM file before analysis.
output_examples.output: A concise report listing modality, image dimensions, transfer syntax, study date, and warnings about patient identifiers.

output_examples.input: A user asks to create research copies of DICOM files.
output: A de-identification checklist for metadata, UIDs, private tags, and burned-in identifiers.
A reminder to verify outputs before sharing outside the care team.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a compressed DICOM image cannot be decoded.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks transfer syntax, optional decoder packages, and fallback conversion options.

best_practices: Verify anonymization with a documented checklist before sharing files.
Keep original DICOM files read-only and write transformed files to a separate directory.
Install only the compression handlers required for the dataset you are processing.
anti_patterns: Sharing converted images without checking for burned-in patient identifiers.
Assuming every DICOM file has the same tags or transfer syntax.
Using metadata exports as de-identified data without reviewing PHI fields.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose medical images?
faq.answer: No. It helps process DICOM data, but clinical interpretation requires qualified medical professionals.

faq.question: Does anonymization make files safe to share?
faq.answer: Not by itself. You must verify metadata, private tags, UIDs, and burned-in identifiers before sharing.

faq.question: Which image formats can it help create?
faq.answer: The helper guidance covers PNG, JPEG, and TIFF conversions from DICOM pixel data.

faq.question: Why do some compressed files fail to open?
faq.answer: Some transfer syntaxes need optional decoder packages such as pylibjpeg, pylibjpeg-openjpeg, or GDCM.

faq.question: Can it process a full imaging series?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for reading folders, sorting slices, and building volume arrays.

faq.question: Is patient metadata exported by default?
faq.answer: The metadata helper can print patient fields. Treat outputs as sensitive unless you redact and review them.
